chunks: That is God's guidance: He gives it to whom He wills of His servants. And if they had associated others with Him, surely vain would have been all they did.
ai.seo_question: What happens to a person's deeds if they commit shirk according to the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse underscores that true guidance (hudā) is not merely intellectual but a divine grace that requires the purity of tawhid; thus, shirk nullifies the spiritual value of all acts of worship. It reflects the principle that the acceptance of deeds is contingent upon correct belief, a key theme in Usul al-Din. The verse serves as a reminder that even abundant good deeds are void if rooted in polytheism, emphasizing the primacy of monotheism in Islamic theology.
